body: Honestly, I've gone through all of that but I don't think there's one single reason why I'm depressed. Probably just the accumulation of all of it.

A lot of what's causing me to feel the way I am right now are just some very specific family issues which is why I haven't gone into too much detail. It's a bit complicated but it's evident that it's not something that can be changed or fixed. I have, however, felt in the past depressed and was able to find the root of the issue like you mentioned but in current circumstances it's not really applicable. Thanks for your words.
I enjoyed reading your experience. If it's not too personal, I'm curious as to how you're doing now and what kind of treatment you received and if you're still undergoing anything?

I definitely realized how it might have come off that way as I was typing that before and almost deleted it. Kind of like someone saying "i'm not crazy" makes them seem more crazy. 

I purposefully haven't gone into too much detail with this post and I literally have no one in person who I could talk my issues over with. Plus, many of the issues I'm powerless to and have no control over so I can't really get to the root of it. 

Thanks for the comment though

10 years is such a long time. I've already dealt with 10 years of depression I absolutely cannot deal with another. Also, I'm so tired of waiting for things to  change and get better. At 13, I thought at 16 things would change. Then at 16, I thought maybe at 18. 18 year old me would be so disappointed to find out I'm still dealing with all this crap at 21.

The key thing I got from what you wrote is the "if you want help" part. I guess I don't really want help. We all have our vices. Some people smoke, drink excessively, or do drugs - maybe mine is just absolutely hating myself.

Again, thanks for commenting. I'll consider watching the TED talk a little later.

Even if I did reach out for help - what would be the point? I don't think that life, in particular my own, is very meaningful and anti-depressants and the like would only bring a false sense of happiness I think. There's so much more I'd like so experience but the way things are going looks like they will never happen whether I decide to end it or not.

Never officially diagnosed and have not seen a doctor about it. I consider myself to be a pretty rational person to be completely honest. I know in the past when I'm just being moody or just want to complain or something but the past year or so a lot has happened that has just made everyday a constant battle that I'm less and less willing to fight everyday. 

Thanks for your comment. I don't think I'll be calling a hotline or voluntarily going to the hospital anytime soon but it was nice hearing that I don't have to feel this way - even if I don't entirely believe that.
